company.text: Perpetual Limited is a Sydney-based group that began as a trustee company in 1886. It grew into funds management, advice and corporate trust; it acquired **Barrow Hanley** and **Trillium** (US) in 2020 and **Pendal Group** (incl. J O Hambro) in 2023. **Corporate Trust** acts as trustee, custodian and manager for securitisation, debt and managed funds, and sells data/software through **Digital & Markets**. In Singapore, Perpetual (Asia) is trustee for S-REITs (it has acted on REIT IPOs since at least 2014, e.g. Frasers Hospitality Trust, Frasers Logistics & Industrial Trust) and for unit trusts. It was appointed trustee for **three new SGX REIT listings** in FY26. Whether Perpetual has any Canadian operations is **to be confirmed** (none found).

financials.country: Australia, listed (ASX: PPT); FY ends 30 June
financials.text:
**FY26 (to June 30, 2026):** operating revenue **A$1,374.2m** (flat); underlying NPAT **A$217.0m** (+6%); statutory NPAT **A$88.9m** (vs a A$58.2m loss in FY25); total dividends **A$1.22/share**. Group AUM **A$224.4bn**, with **A$25.1bn net outflows**. **Corporate Trust:** revenue **A$220.8m** (+8%), underlying PBT **A$98.8m** (+9%), FUA **A$1,349.3bn** (+6%); **Singapore** Managed Funds FUA **A$75.3bn** (+11%). Simplification program delivered **A$72.6m** of annualised cost savings; gross debt down 15% to A$629.3m.

**Restructuring history:** In May 2024 Perpetual agreed to sell **Wealth Management and Corporate Trust to KKR** (about **A$2.2bn**). The deal was **terminated in February 2025** after a tax ruling cut expected proceeds and an independent expert found it was not in shareholders' interests (A$21m break-fee dispute). Wealth Management is now being sold on its own to **Bain Capital** (signed March 2026, **A$500m** upfront plus up to A$50m earnout; completion expected **end of 2026**). **EQT** made several non-binding proposals for the company in July to September 2026 (up to A$22.50/share); the board **rejected the 'best and final' proposal on Sept 21, 2026** and ended talks. **Corporate Trust is being kept** as a core business.

industry.title: Trustee and fund services go digital
industry.text: Trustees are partnering with custodians and fund administrators (e.g. Perpetual with Northern Trust in Singapore) and investing in data and automation: talent-heavy work that suits a lower-cost, tech-rich hub.

industry.title: T+1 and North American hours
industry.text: US and Canadian markets moved to **T+1 settlement**, which favours operations teams working in Eastern Time. Montréal shares New York's time zone.

industry.title: Montréal's fund-services cluster
industry.text: State Street, Maples Group, BNP Paribas, Société Générale, Morgan Stanley and others run operations in Montréal; the **ISSB** chose Montréal as its Americas headquarters.

industry.title: Perpetual in simplification mode
industry.text: After the KKR collapse, the Bain sale and the EQT approaches, management is focused on **costs and two core businesses**. A Montréal case must be framed as **efficiency and growth**, not just expansion.

talking_points: How does Corporate Trust serve clients in **North American hours** today, and is there demand from US/Canadian managers or Perpetual's **US boutiques** (Barrow Hanley, Trillium)?
Where does Perpetual plan to place **digital and data** talent as Corporate Trust invests in its transformation?
Would a **small pilot team** (registry, fund accounting support, compliance, data) in Montréal fit the post-sale cost agenda, given the **24% IFC salary credit**?
Who owns location decisions for Corporate Trust: Matt, the **SVP Sales**, the **Country MD**, or Sydney group executives?
Can Finance Montréal set up **introductions** (Maples Group, State Street, Mila) or a **Montréal visit** for his team?
